name: Écru et noir
why: The airy ecru linen shirt balances the black pleated trouser; loafers keep a warm-weather date relaxed.
avoid: No extra belt; press the linen lightly, do not add a shiny blazer.

name: Noir et indigo
why: The nearly black shirt and indigo jeans work if the navy/black contrast is deliberate; black loafers keep the leather temperature coherent.
avoid: Verify the shirt color in natural light: the receipt says brown, while the product photo reads black; avoid this look until confirmed.

name: Jacquard tranquille
why: The ecru wrap-style overshirt is the single statement; its self-tie defines the waist against quiet black pleats and loafers.
avoid: Wear closed; an open version would need an additional base layer not pictured. No second belt or competing pattern.

name: Chemise noire
why: A black crochet-texture shirt and pleated trouser share a dark palette; suede boots add a third surface.
avoid: If the crochet is translucent, wear a tonal underlayer; no exposed belt.

name: Olive et noir
why: Muted olive at the face, black pleats and suede boots read quietly Parisian; dark wool coat for the cool walk.
avoid: Do not add a patterned scarf to the olive neckline.

name: Nuit déstructurée
why: The seam on this black shirt supplies detail while matte trouser cloth and suede boots differentiate the blacks.
avoid: No separate belt or shiny metal.

name: Lacets et écru
why: Black lace-neck knit is the focal point; black pleats and suede Chelsea boots give it a sharp cool-evening silhouette.
avoid: Dry autumn or spring evening; no belt, no second statement.

name: Rive gauche
why: Narrow burgundy stripe against clean black tailoring is a restrained point of interest; loafers soften the register.
avoid: Skip a second print or shiny jewelry.

name: Brun et anthracite
why: Textured brown shirt, plain black pleats and loafers make a muted dinner outfit; the dark wool coat adds depth without a second pattern.
avoid: One open collar button; do not mix the checked shirt with pinstripe trousers.

name: Col ouvert, laine
why: The subtle cream micro-grid shirt lightens charcoal pinstriped trousers; dark coat and black loafers ground the look.
avoid: Keep the shirt softly open rather than adding a tie. Check the semi-sheer shirt under strong light.

name: Rayure discrète
why: Fine warm vertical stripes and discreet charcoal pinstripes can work when the stripe scales differ; black loafers and dark wool coat keep it relaxed.
avoid: Check the two stripe scales in daylight; if they compete, use subtly textured cream shirt #39.
stylist_note: Only one relaxed detail: one collar button undone, no extra scarf.

name: Chemise ivoire légère
why: A soft ecru cotton-linen shirt sits above black pleats and loafers for warm-weather café or casual coworking.
avoid: Photo looks like a shirt, not a polo; do not treat this as a business suit look.

name: Indigo sous laine
why: Dark denim shirt with black pleats and loafers keeps the workwear reference subtle; wool coat smartens the commute.
avoid: Coworking rather than conservative client meeting; never blue denim-on-denim.

name: Un col noir
why: Black shirt and charcoal pinstripe trouser with loafers make a creative-office uniform; dark wool coat adds dimension.
avoid: No matching pinstripe blazer over a black shirt for corporate meetings.

name: Costume gris (smart-casual)
why: A matched grey jacket and trousers with a pale shirt and brown derbies is a usable smart-casual event combination, subject to fit.
avoid: For strict black-tie or formal ceremonies, wear the black Suitsupply suit with proper shirt instead. Check the semi-sheer shirt under strong light. If its transparency shows under event lighting, switch to a verified opaque dress shirt.

name: Crème sur anthracite
why: An off-white short-sleeve jacquard shirt is a spring/summer dinner contrast against charcoal pinstripe trousers; black loafers keep it informal.
avoid: No graphic layer or duplicate check jacket.

name: Chemise d’été
why: Linen on crinkled drawstring trousers is a coherent summer-weight pairing; loafers keep it composed.
avoid: Both pieces are loose: tuck only the front if the proportions balloon; no belt.

name: Chemise d’été ivoire
why: The ecru shirt with off-white wide drawstring trousers is a deliberate summery tonal look; black loafers ground it.
avoid: Check shades of ecru and white in daylight; if they clash, wear black pleats instead.

name: Rayure fine et noir
why: Off-white tonal jacquard and black pleats form an easy café look with no extra accessories.
avoid: No second print or suit jacket on a hot day.

name: Week-end olive
why: An olive henley and dark denim with brown leather give a warm autumn palette without a graphic or logo.
avoid: Dark/even wash only; change shoes if the pavement is wet.

name: Chemise brun foncé
why: The textured brown shirt relates naturally to dark denim and brown shoes; no black leather enters the outfit.
avoid: The brown shirt is not a business dress shirt.

name: Denim noir équilibré
why: Black denim overshirt over black pleats with suede Chelsea boots is a textured weekend dark look without double denim or mixed leather.
avoid: Do not combine this overshirt with another denim layer; no belt needed.

name: Graphique hors ville
why: The owned graphic tee can be styled for errands with dark denim; this is honest off-duty coverage, not a Parisian outfit recommendation.
avoid: Gym/errands only; never dinner, date or office.

name: Riverside hors ville
why: Graphic collegiate tee stays in the off-duty lane; dark jeans and brown shoes keep the rest simple.
avoid: Not a city-style recommendation or dinner look.

name: Momo hors ville
why: The printed tank is an underlayer for a zipped black bomber and black pleats; avoid showing the slogan.
avoid: Off-duty only, not an elegant look; cover the tank.

name: Vert graphique hors ville
why: The washed charcoal slogan tee belongs outside the Parisian capsule; zipped bomber hides the print on short errands.
avoid: Do not treat this as a date, work, club or smart outfit.

name: Chemise à carreaux
why: A larger brown check is the sole pattern; dark denim and matching brown leather make it a weekend outfit.
avoid: No striped jacket or pinstriped trouser with this shirt.

name: Jean blouson
why: A faded-blue denim overshirt goes over clean black pleats: no double denim and no competing logos.
avoid: Light denim is weekend-only; the closure type is unverified.

name: Écru décontracté
why: The washed fluid shirt is the only patterned piece; black pleats and loafers quiet it down.
avoid: Keep this soft viscose out of autumn/winter; no pinstriped blazer.

name: Débardeur couvert
why: Plain white tank is a summer underlayer, not a standalone Parisian top; ecru relaxed jacket and black pleats add coverage.
avoid: Check ecru jacket against optical white tank in daylight; if stark, skip this combination.

name: Blanc sous denim
why: The white tank stays covered by dark denim shirt-jacket; black pleats and loafers keep the outline neat.
avoid: Weekend only; denim shirt worn open, not buttoned shut over the tank.

name: Gris sous denim
why: Grey ribbed tank stays beneath a black denim overshirt; black pleats and suede boots keep texture varied.
avoid: No standalone tank in city; verify overshirt coverage.

name: Maille sous denim
why: Grey ribbed tank works only as a covered base; dark denim overshirt and black pleats create a low-key weekend uniform.
avoid: Not a smart event; never leave the tank as the only top.

name: Noir sans logo
why: Black crochet shirt and relaxed black pleated trousers gain texture from suede Chelsea boots; no accessories swing on the dance floor.
avoid: Ensure open knit has a tonal base, no exposed silver chain.

name: Détails cousus
why: Seam detail on the black shirt under a matte black bomber gives a late-night layer, while suede boots add depth to black pleats.
avoid: Bomber should be matte, not shiny; leave it in the cloakroom once inside. No exposed belt.

name: Noir souple
why: The textured black shirt, wide black pleats, black linen-blend blazer and suede boots make a deliberate night look with distinct surfaces.
avoid: Wide-on-wide cut must fit shoulders and waist; no shiny metal or visible belt.

name: Écru souple
why: Light ecru linen shirt breaks up the black relaxed blazer and pleated trouser while black loafers keep the palette tight.
avoid: Spring/summer only; check the two black suit separates for matching depth and fit.

name: Indigo léger
why: Off-white thin-striped shirt and dark indigo jeans form an easy weekend look; black loafers elevate the shoes.
avoid: No pinstriped jacket over the stripe and no oversized tote at dinner.

name: Noir sans emphase
why: Black structured shirt, relaxed black pleats and suede boots make a dark weekend base with contrast in surface, not color.
avoid: Hem the trousers if they pool; faded black layers will not work.

name: Écru anthracite
why: A relaxed ecru linen shirt softens charcoal pinstripe trousers; black loafers prevent a formal-suit read.
avoid: Spring evenings only: linen is wrong in cold weather; avoid the matching pinstripe jacket.
